## L2-030: Per-Package Service Registration
**Traces to:** L1-006

Each generator package must expose a single `IServiceCollection` extension method
(`AddCoreServices`, `AddDotNetServices`, `AddAngularServices`, `AddPythonServices`,
`AddReactServices`, `AddReactNativeServices`, `AddFlaskServices`, `AddPlaywrightServices`,
`AddDetoxServices`, `AddScaffoldingServices`) that registers all of that package's
strategies and services.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a service collection with only `AddCoreServices` called, when `IArtifactGenerator`
   is resolved, then resolution must succeed.
2. Given `AddFlaskServices` has been called, when `ISyntaxGenerationStrategy<ControllerModel>`
   is resolved, then at least one Flask controller strategy must be returned.
3. Given `AddCoreServices(assembly)` is called with a consumer assembly, when strategies
   defined in that assembly are resolved, then they must be registered as singletons
   without further configuration.
4. Given a package registration method is called twice, when services are resolved, then
   duplicate registrations must not cause resolution to fail.

---

## L2-031: .NET Solution and Project Scaffolding
**Traces to:** L1-007

The system must generate a solution file, its projects, and their project references.
Both `.sln` and `.slnx` solution formats must be supported, selected by the `--slnx`
option or the `slnx` configuration key.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a `SolutionModel` with two projects, when it is generated, then a solution file and
   both project directories with `.csproj` files must exist on disk.
2. Given `--slnx` is supplied, when the solution is created, then the solution file must
   carry the `.slnx` extension and be created using the XML-based solution format.
3. Given a project declaring a reference to another project in the same solution, when it is
   generated, then the `.csproj` must contain a matching `ProjectReference`.
4. Given a target framework of `net8.0`, when projects are generated, then each `.csproj`
   must declare `net8.0` as its `TargetFramework`.

---

## L2-032: C# Syntax Generation Breadth
**Traces to:** L1-007

The .NET package must generate C# classes, interfaces, records, enums, methods,
constructors, properties, fields, parameters, attributes, namespaces, expressions,
documents, controllers, and controller methods, and must support DDD constructs
(entities, aggregates, value objects, domain events, specifications) and CQRS constructs
(commands, queries, handlers, validators).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a `ClassModel` with a public modifier, four properties, and one attribute, when it
   is generated, then the emitted C# must declare the class with the attribute applied and
   all four properties.
2. Given a CQRS command model, when it is generated, then a request type, a handler
   implementing the MediatR handler interface, and a validator must be produced.
3. Given an entity model with a domain event, when it is generated, then the entity must
   raise the declared event.
4. Given a controller model with four actions, when it is generated, then the emitted
   controller must declare four routed action methods.
5. Given any generated C# file, when it is compiled, then it must compile without syntax
   errors.

---

## L2-033: Full-Stack Application Scaffolding
**Traces to:** L1-007

`IFullStackFactory.CreateAsync(FullStackCreateOptions)` must produce a `FullStackModel`
containing a solution, an optional backend project, and an optional frontend project, from
a name and output directory alone.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `FullStackCreateOptions` with a name and directory, when `CreateAsync` is called,
   then the returned model's `Solution` must be non-null and rooted at the supplied
   directory.
2. Given the returned `FullStackModel` is passed to `IArtifactGenerator.GenerateAsync`, when
   generation completes, then the solution directory must contain both backend and frontend
   project directories.
3. Given a supplied `FrontendProjectName`, when the model is created, then the frontend
   project must carry that name.

---

## L2-034: JWT-Authenticated MVP Scaffolding
**Traces to:** L1-007

`IJwtAuthenticatedMvpFactory.GenerateAsync(JwtAuthenticatedMvpOptions, CancellationToken)`
must scaffold a JWT-authenticated full-stack solution from an embedded template manifest,
rendering root-scoped templates once, `_entity/`-scoped templates once per declared entity,
and `_page/`-scoped templates once per declared page.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given options with an empty `Name`, when `GenerateAsync` is called, then
   `ArgumentException` must be thrown naming the options parameter and no file must be
   written.
2. Given options with an empty `Directory`, when `GenerateAsync` is called, then
   `ArgumentException` must be thrown and no file must be written.
3. Given options declaring entities `Order` and `Customer`, when generation completes, then
   every `_entity/` template must have produced one output per entity with entity-scoped
   tokens (`Entity`, `EntityLower`, `EntityKebab`, `EntityProperties`) bound.
4. Given options declaring a page with `RequiresAuth` set to `true`, when generation
   completes, then the generated route for that page must be guarded by authentication.
5. Given a cancellation token cancelled mid-manifest, when generation continues, then
   `OperationCanceledException` must be thrown and remaining templates must not render.
6. Given the embedded template manifest is missing or empty, when `GenerateAsync` is called,
   then a warning must be logged and the call must complete without throwing.

---

## L2-035: Git Repository Integration
**Traces to:** L1-007

The system must be able to initialize a Git repository for generated output and perform
repository operations through `IGitService`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a `GitModel` targeting a generated solution directory, when it is generated, then
   that directory must contain an initialized Git repository.
2. Given a scaffold configuration with `gitInit` set to `true`, when scaffolding completes,
   then the output root must contain an initialized Git repository.
3. Given `gitInit` is `false` or absent, when scaffolding completes, then no repository must
   be initialized.

---

## L2-036: API Contract and BDD Artifact Generation
**Traces to:** L1-007

The .NET package must generate OpenAPI documents, SpecFlow feature files, and SignalR hubs
and clients from their respective models.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an `OpenApiDocumentModel` describing three endpoints, when it is generated, then a
   valid OpenAPI document declaring all three paths must be produced.
2. Given a `SpecFlowFeatureFileModel` with two scenarios, when it is generated, then a
   `.feature` file in Gherkin syntax containing both scenarios must be produced.
3. Given a SignalR hub model, when it is generated, then both a server hub class and a
   corresponding client must be produced.

---

## L2-037: Schema Format Detection
**Traces to:** L1-008

`ISchemaFormatDetector.Detect(content, filePath)` must identify PlantUML, OpenAPI, JSON
Schema, Proto, and Avro inputs from the file extension first and the content otherwise, and
must fail explicitly when no format can be determined.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a file path ending in `.puml`, when detection runs, then `SchemaFormat.PlantUml`
   must be returned regardless of content.
2. Given content beginning with `@startuml` and no file path, when detection runs, then
   `SchemaFormat.PlantUml` must be returned.
3. Given content containing `"openapi"`, when detection runs, then `SchemaFormat.OpenApi`
   must be returned.
4. Given content containing `"$schema"` and `json-schema.org`, when detection runs, then
   `SchemaFormat.JsonSchema` must be returned.
5. Given content matching no known format and no recognizable extension, when detection
   runs, then `SchemaFormatDetectionException` must be thrown.

---

## L2-038: Normalized Schema Model
**Traces to:** L1-008

Every supported schema format must normalize into a single `NormalizedSchema` carrying
entities (with stereotype, properties, and methods), relationships (with type and
cardinality), endpoints (with method, parameters, request and response types, and
authentication requirement), and the originating source format.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a JSON Schema with one object definition of three properties, when it is
   normalized, then the result must contain one entity with three properties and
   `SourceFormat` equal to `JsonSchema`.
2. Given a schema property marked required, when it is normalized, then the corresponding
   `NormalizedProperty.IsRequired` must be `true`.
3. Given an array-valued property, when it is normalized, then `IsCollection` must be `true`
   and `CollectionItemType` must name the item type.
4. Given an OpenAPI operation requiring a security scheme, when it is normalized, then the
   corresponding endpoint's `RequiresAuthentication` must be `true`.

---

## L2-039: PlantUML Parsing and Validation
**Traces to:** L1-008

`IPlantUmlParserService` must parse PlantUML class and sequence diagrams,
`IPlantUmlValidationService` must reject malformed diagrams before parsing, and
`IPlantUmlSolutionModelFactory` must turn a parsed diagram into a solution model.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a PlantUML class diagram declaring two classes and one association, when it is
   parsed, then two entities and one relationship must be produced.
2. Given a PlantUML document missing `@enduml`, when it is validated, then validation must
   fail with a message identifying the malformed document.
3. Given a valid sequence diagram, when it is converted, then a solution model containing a
   project per participant must be produced.

---

## L2-040: YAML Configuration Parsing
**Traces to:** L1-009

`IYamlConfigParser.Parse(yaml)` must deserialize a scaffold configuration and must raise
`ScaffoldParseException` on malformed YAML. A parse failure must be reported as a
validation error against the `yaml` property with error code `SCAFFOLD_PARSE_FAILED` and
must not begin scaffolding.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given syntactically invalid YAML, when `ScaffoldAsync` is called, then the result must
   carry a validation error on property `yaml`, one error with code
   `SCAFFOLD_PARSE_FAILED`, and no file must be written.
2. Given valid YAML, when it is parsed, then the resulting `ScaffoldConfiguration` must
   carry the declared name, version, output path, global variables, projects, and solutions.
3. Given valid YAML, when `Validate(yaml)` is called, then parsing and validation must run
   without writing any file.

---

## L2-041: Scaffold Root Validation
**Traces to:** L1-009

A scaffold configuration must declare a non-empty `name`, a `version` matching semantic
versioning (`major.minor.patch` with optional prerelease and build metadata), and at least
one project.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a configuration with an empty `name`, when it is validated, then an error must be
   reported on property `name`.
2. Given `version: "1.0"`, when the configuration is validated, then an error must be
   reported on `version` identifying the invalid semver format.
3. Given `version: "1.0.0-beta.1+build.7"`, when the configuration is validated, then no
   version error must be reported.
4. Given a configuration with an empty `projects` list, when it is validated, then an error
   must be reported on `projects`.

---

## L2-042: Scaffold Project and Reference Validation
**Traces to:** L1-009

Every project must declare a name and a path; project names must be unique
case-insensitively; every project reference and every solution project reference must
resolve to a declared project.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given two projects named `Api` and `api`, when the configuration is validated, then a
   duplicate-name error must be reported.
2. Given a project with no `path`, when the configuration is validated, then an error must
   be reported on that project's `path`.
3. Given a project referencing `Domain` where no project named `Domain` is declared, when
   the configuration is validated, then an error must be reported naming the unresolved
   reference.
4. Given a solution listing a project that is not declared, when the configuration is
   validated, then an error must be reported naming the solution and the missing project.

---

## L2-043: File Definition Content Source Exclusivity
**Traces to:** L1-009

A file definition must declare a name and at most one content source among `content`,
`template`, and `source`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a file declaring both `content` and `template`, when the configuration is
   validated, then an error must be reported stating that exactly one of content, template,
   or source is permitted.
2. Given a file with no `name`, when the configuration is validated, then an error must be
   reported on the file's `name`.
3. Given a file declaring only `template`, when the configuration is validated, then no file
   error must be reported.

---

## L2-044: Architecture Resolution
**Traces to:** L1-009

`IArchitectureResolver` must expand a project's declared architecture into concrete layers:
`clean-architecture` into Domain, Application, Infrastructure, and Api layers with
Domain ← Application ← Infrastructure and Api → (Application, Infrastructure) references;
`vertical-slices` into a single web API project; any project declaring explicit `layers`
into those custom layers; and anything else into the `none` pattern.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a project named `Shop` with `architecture: clean-architecture`, when it is
   resolved, then four layers named `Shop.Domain`, `Shop.Application`,
   `Shop.Infrastructure`, and `Shop.Api` must be produced at paths under `src/`.
2. Given the same project, when the resolved layers are inspected, then `Shop.Application`
   must reference `Shop.Domain`, `Shop.Infrastructure` must reference `Shop.Application`,
   and `Shop.Api` must reference both `Shop.Application` and `Shop.Infrastructure`.
3. Given a clean-architecture project declaring entities, endpoints, and services, when it
   is resolved, then entities must be assigned to the Domain layer, endpoints to the Api
   layer, and services to the Infrastructure layer.
4. Given `architecture: vertical-slices`, when it is resolved, then exactly one
   `dotnet-webapi` layer carrying the project's entities, services, and endpoints must be
   produced.
5. Given no architecture and no layers, when the project is resolved, then the resolved
   pattern must be `none`.

---

## L2-045: Scaffold Output Path Resolution
**Traces to:** L1-009

The scaffold output root must be resolved as: the supplied output directory (made absolute
against the current directory when relative), then the configuration's `outputPath` when it
is set and not `.`, then the configuration `name`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given output directory `./out`, `outputPath: dist`, and `name: Shop`, when scaffolding
   runs, then files must be written under `<cwd>/out/dist/Shop`.
2. Given an absolute output directory, when scaffolding runs, then the current directory
   must not be prepended.
3. Given `outputPath: "."`, when scaffolding runs, then the resolved root must be
   `<output>/<name>` with no intermediate segment.

---

## L2-046: Post-Scaffold Command Execution
**Traces to:** L1-009

Post-scaffold commands must run only when the run is not a dry run, must execute in the
resolved output root, and must not abort the run when one fails; each failure must be
recorded with error code `SCAFFOLD_POST_CMD_FAILED` and logged as a warning naming the
command and exit code.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a configuration with two post-scaffold commands where the first exits non-zero,
   when scaffolding runs, then the second command must still execute and one error with
   code `SCAFFOLD_POST_CMD_FAILED` must be recorded.
2. Given `--dry-run`, when scaffolding runs, then no post-scaffold command must be executed.
3. Given a failing post-scaffold command, when the run completes, then a warning naming the
   command and its exit code must be written to the console.

---

## L2-047: Schema Export and Configuration Bootstrapping
**Traces to:** L1-009

The `scaffold` command must support `--export-schema`, which writes the configuration JSON
Schema to standard output, and `--init`, which writes a starter `scaffold.yaml` into the
output directory. Both must return without scaffolding.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `scaffold --export-schema`, when the command runs, then a JSON Schema document must
   be written to standard output and no file must be created.
2. Given `scaffold --init -o ./out`, when the command runs, then `./out/scaffold.yaml` must
   exist and its path must be logged.
3. Given the file produced by `--init`, when it is passed to `scaffold --validate`, then
   validation must pass.

---

## L2-048: Root Command — Create Code Generator Project
**Traces to:** L1-010

The root command must create a new code-generator CLI solution from `--name`,
`--output`, `--framework`, `--slnx`, `--local-source-root`, `--diagnostics`, and
`--fail-fast`. It must validate options before writing, create the solution and project
directories, generate the `.csproj`, the command sources, and the install script, and add
the project to the solution.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `-n MyGen -o ./out`, when the command completes, then `./out/MyGen` must contain a
   solution file, `src/MyGen.Cli/MyGen.Cli.csproj`, `Program.cs`, and a `Commands`
   directory containing `AppRootCommand.cs`, `HelloWorldCommand.cs`, and
   `EnterpriseSolutionCommand.cs`.
2. Given the same invocation, when the command completes, then
   `eng/scripts/install-cli.bat` must exist.
3. Given `--local-source-root <path>`, when the `.csproj` is generated, then it must contain
   `ProjectReference` entries relative to that path instead of `PackageReference` entries.
4. Given no `--local-source-root`, when the `.csproj` is generated, then it must contain
   `PackageReference` entries for all nine CodeGenerator packages at the versions declared
   in `PackageVersions`.
5. Given the generated solution, when `dotnet build` is run against it, then the build must
   succeed.

---

## L2-049: Install Command
**Traces to:** L1-010

`create-code-cli install [-o <dir>]` must write a Claude skill file to
`<dir>/.claude/skills/code-generator/SKILL.md`, creating intermediate directories, and must
log the written path.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `install -o ./proj` where `.claude` does not exist, when the command runs, then
   `./proj/.claude/skills/code-generator/SKILL.md` must exist.
2. Given no `-o`, when the command runs, then the skill must be written under the current
   working directory.
3. Given the written file, when it is inspected, then it must begin with YAML front matter
   declaring `name: code-generator`.

---

## L2-050: Scaffold Command Option Surface
**Traces to:** L1-010

The `scaffold` command must accept `--config`, `--output`, `--dry-run`, `--force`,
`--validate`, `--export-schema`, `--init`, `--diagnostics`, and `--fail-fast`. When
`--config` is omitted it must default to `scaffold.yaml` in the output directory, and must
report a clear error when no configuration can be located.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given no `--config` and a `scaffold.yaml` present in the output directory, when the
   command runs, then that file must be used.
2. Given no `--config`, no `scaffold.yaml`, and a non-interactive session, when the command
   runs, then an error stating that no configuration file was found must be logged and no
   file must be written.
3. Given `--config` pointing at a non-existent path, when the command runs, then an error
   naming that path must be logged.
4. Given `--validate`, when the command runs, then only parsing and validation must occur
   and no file must be written.

---

## L2-051: Global Verbose Option
**Traces to:** L1-010

A global `--verbose` / `-v` option must raise the minimum log level to `Debug` and cause
stack traces to be included in error output. It must be honoured even when the failure
occurs before command parsing completes.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `--verbose`, when the CLI starts, then the configured minimum log level must be
   `Debug`.
2. Given no verbose flag, when the CLI starts, then the configured minimum log level must be
   `Information`.
3. Given `--verbose` and a failing command, when the error is written, then the exception
   stack trace must appear in standard error.
4. Given no verbose flag and a failing command, when the error is written, then no stack
   trace must appear.

---

## L2-052: Shell Completion
**Traces to:** L1-010

The CLI must supply completions for the framework, name, and output options, and must
detect the active shell (PowerShell, zsh, bash, fish) from the environment, defaulting to
PowerShell on Windows and bash elsewhere.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a completion request for `--framework` with the partial text `net9`, when
   completions are produced, then `net9.0` must be among them.
2. Given a completion request for `--output`, when completions are produced, then at most 20
   subdirectories of the current directory must be returned.
3. Given `PSModulePath` is set in the environment, when the shell is detected, then
   `powershell` must be returned.
4. Given `SHELL` contains `zsh`, when the shell is detected, then `zsh` must be returned.
5. Given the output directory cannot be enumerated, when completions are requested, then an
   empty set must be returned rather than an exception.

---

## L2-053: Generated Starter Project Contract
**Traces to:** L1-010

The generated starter CLI project must be packable as a .NET global tool with
`ToolCommandName` set to the lower-cased solution name suffixed with `-cli`, must register
all generator packages in `Program.cs`, and must expose working `hello` and
`enterprise-solution` commands.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a generated project named `MyGen`, when its `.csproj` is inspected, then
   `PackAsTool` must be `true` and `ToolCommandName` must be `mygen-cli`.
2. Given the generated `Program.cs`, when it is inspected, then it must call
   `AddCoreServices` plus every language package registration method.
3. Given the generated project is built and run with `hello -o ./out`, when execution
   completes, then `./out/HelloWorld.txt` must exist.
4. Given the generated project is run with `enterprise-solution -n Sample -o ./out`, when
   execution completes, then a solution must be produced under `./out`.

---

## L2-054: Four-Tier Configuration Precedence
**Traces to:** L1-011

Configuration must be resolved from four tiers applied in order — built-in defaults, then
the configuration file, then environment variables, then CLI arguments — with later tiers
overriding earlier ones. Key lookup must be case-insensitive. Built-in defaults must be
`framework=net9.0`, `output=.`, and `slnx=false`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given no file, environment, or CLI value, when `framework` is read, then `net9.0` must be
   returned.
2. Given `.codegenerator.json` sets `framework` to `net8.0` and `CODEGEN_FRAMEWORK` is
   unset, when `framework` is read, then `net8.0` must be returned.
3. Given the file sets `framework` to `net8.0` and `CODEGEN_FRAMEWORK` is `net9.0`, when
   `framework` is read, then `net9.0` must be returned.
4. Given all three tiers set `framework` and `--framework net10.0` is supplied, when the
   effective value is used, then `net10.0` must win.
5. Given a key registered as `Framework`, when it is read as `framework`, then the value
   must be returned.
6. Given a key prefixed `templates.`, when `GetSection("templates")` is called, then the
   returned dictionary must contain the key with the prefix removed.

---

## L2-055: Configuration File Discovery
**Traces to:** L1-011

`IConfigurationLoader.LoadAsync(directory)` must search for `.codegenerator.json` starting
at the supplied directory and walking upward to the filesystem root, returning the first
match, and must return an empty configuration when none is found.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `.codegenerator.json` in the starting directory, when configuration is loaded, then
   that file must be used.
2. Given `.codegenerator.json` two directories above the starting directory and none below,
   when configuration is loaded, then the ancestor file must be used.
3. Given no `.codegenerator.json` anywhere in the ancestor chain, when configuration is
   loaded, then an empty configuration must be returned and no exception must be thrown.
4. Given a `.codegenerator.json` with property names in differing case, when it is
   deserialized, then property matching must be case-insensitive.

---

## L2-056: Environment Variable Mapping
**Traces to:** L1-011

The environment tier must map `CODEGEN_FRAMEWORK` → `framework`, `CODEGEN_OUTPUT` →
`output`, `CODEGEN_SLNX` → `slnx`, `CODEGEN_AUTHOR` → `templates.author`, and
`CODEGEN_LICENSE` → `templates.license`. Unset variables must contribute no key.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `CODEGEN_OUTPUT=/tmp/gen`, when the environment tier is mapped, then the tier must
   contain `output` = `/tmp/gen`.
2. Given `CODEGEN_AUTHOR=Ada`, when the environment tier is mapped, then the tier must
   contain `templates.author` = `Ada`.
3. Given none of the recognized variables are set, when the environment tier is mapped, then
   the resulting dictionary must be empty and must not overwrite lower tiers.

---

## L2-057: CLI Option Validation Rules
**Traces to:** L1-012

Generation options must be validated before any directory is created: `Name` must be
non-empty and a valid C# namespace identifier; `Framework` must be non-empty and begin with
`net`; and the parent of `OutputDirectory` must exist. Failure must raise
`CliValidationException`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `-n "My-Gen"`, when validation runs, then an error must be reported on `Name`
   stating it is not a valid C# identifier, and no directory must be created.
2. Given `-n ""`, when validation runs, then an error must be reported on `Name` stating it
   is required.
3. Given `-f "dotnet9"`, when validation runs, then an error must be reported on `Framework`
   stating it must start with `net`.
4. Given an output directory whose parent does not exist, when validation runs, then an
   error must be reported on `OutputDirectory`.
5. Given any validation error, when the CLI terminates, then the process exit code must be
   `1`.

---

## L2-058: Warnings Are Non-Blocking
**Traces to:** L1-012

Validation warnings must be reported without preventing the operation. A solution name
longer than 128 characters must produce a warning about filesystem limits, not an error.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a valid name of 200 characters, when validation runs, then the result must be valid
   and must contain one warning on `Name`.
2. Given the same input, when the command runs, then generation must proceed and the warning
   must be written to the log with its property name and message.
3. Given a result containing only warnings, when `IsValid` is evaluated, then it must be
   `true`.

---

## L2-059: JSON Schema Input Validation
**Traces to:** L1-012

`IInputValidator.Validate(input, jsonSchema)` must validate arbitrary structured input
against a registered JSON Schema and must report each schema violation with the offending
property path. Schema failures must map to error code `SCHEMA_INVALID`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given input missing a property the schema marks required, when validation runs, then the
   result must be invalid and must name that property.
2. Given input whose property type conflicts with the schema, when validation runs, then the
   result must be invalid and must name that property.
3. Given input satisfying the schema, when validation runs, then the result must be valid
   with no errors.
4. Given a schema identifier that is not registered, when validation is requested, then the
   failure must be reported with error code `SCHEMA_INVALID`.

---

## L2-060: Fluent Validation Engine
**Traces to:** L1-012

`Validator<T>` must support property rules via expressions (`RuleFor`), whole-object rules
(`Must`), and conditional rule groups (`When`), and must accumulate every failure rather
than stopping at the first.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a validator with three failing rules, when `Validate` is called, then the result
   must contain three errors.
2. Given `RuleFor(x => x.Name, ...)`, when the rule fails, then the reported property name
   must be `Name`.
3. Given `When(false, ...)` wrapping a failing rule, when `Validate` is called, then that
   rule must not be evaluated and must not contribute an error.
4. Given `Must(...)` fails, when the result is inspected, then the error must be reported
   with an empty property name.

---

## L2-061: Exit Code Taxonomy
**Traces to:** L1-013

The CLI must terminate with a stable exit code identifying the failure class: `0` success,
`1` validation, `2` I/O, `3` process, `4` template, `5` configuration, `6` plugin, `7`
schema, `8` cancelled, `99` unexpected.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a successful run, when the process exits, then the exit code must be `0`.
2. Given a validation failure, when the process exits, then the exit code must be `1`.
3. Given the user presses Ctrl+C, when the process exits, then the exit code must be `8` and
   `Operation cancelled.` must be written to standard error.
4. Given an unhandled non-CLI exception, when the process exits, then the exit code must be
   `99` and a message tagged `[INTERNAL]` must be written to standard error.

---

## L2-062: Typed Exception Hierarchy
**Traces to:** L1-013

Every anticipated failure must be expressed as a `CliException` subtype carrying its exit
code: `CliValidationException`, `CliIOException`, `CliProcessException`,
`CliTemplateException`, `CliConfigurationException`, `CliPluginException`,
`CliSchemaException`, `CliCancelledException`, and `CliAggregateException`. An aggregate's
exit code must be the maximum of its inner exceptions' exit codes.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a `CliTemplateException`, when its exit code is read, then it must be `4`.
2. Given a `CliAggregateException` wrapping a validation (`1`) and a plugin (`6`) exception,
   when its exit code is read, then it must be `6`.
3. Given a `CliAggregateException` is thrown, when the CLI handles it, then every inner
   exception must be formatted and written to standard error.
4. Given a `CliAggregateException` constructed with no inner exceptions, when its exit code
   is read, then it must be `99`.

---

## L2-063: Stable Error Code Catalog
**Traces to:** L1-013

Every reported error must carry a stable code drawn from the published catalog
(`VALIDATION_*`, `IO_*`, `TEMPLATE_*`, `SCAFFOLD_*`, `PROCESS_*`, `PLUGIN_*`, `SCHEMA_*`,
`CONFIG_*`, `INTERNAL_UNEXPECTED`) and a category from `ErrorCategory`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a template that cannot be located, when the error is produced, then its code must
   be `TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`.
2. Given a strategy that throws, when the error is produced, then its code must be
   `PLUGIN_STRATEGY_EXEC_FAILED`.
3. Given a post-scaffold command that exits non-zero, when the error is produced, then its
   code must be `SCAFFOLD_POST_CMD_FAILED` and its category must be `Process`.
4. Given any produced `ErrorInfo`, when it is inspected, then its code must be non-empty.

---

## L2-064: Multi-Format Error Rendering
**Traces to:** L1-013

Errors, validation results, artifact results, and scaffold results must be renderable as
plain console text, JSON, and Markdown through a common `IErrorFormatter` abstraction.
Stack traces must appear only in verbose mode.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an `ErrorInfo`, when the console formatter renders it, then the output must be
   `ERROR [<code>] <message>`.
2. Given the same error, when the JSON formatter renders it, then the output must be valid
   JSON with camel-cased `code`, `message`, `severity`, and `category` members.
3. Given an invalid `ValidationResult`, when the console formatter renders it, then each
   error must appear on its own line prefixed by its property name, and each warning must be
   prefixed `WARNING`.
4. Given a `CliException` and `verbose = false`, when it is formatted, then the stack trace
   must be omitted; given `verbose = true`, it must be included.
5. Given a `ScaffoldResult`, when it is formatted, then the summary must state success or
   failure, planned file count, error count, and duration.

---

## L2-065: Rollback Change Tracking
**Traces to:** L1-014

`IGenerationRollbackService` must track created files, modified files (capturing a backup
copy at the moment of tracking), deleted files (with their backup), and created
directories, so that each can be reversed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an existing file is tracked as modified, when tracking occurs, then a backup copy of
   its pre-change content must be created.
2. Given a file is tracked as created, when rollback runs, then the file must be deleted and
   recorded in the report's `FilesDeleted`.
3. Given a file tracked as modified, when rollback runs, then its original content must be
   restored, the backup must be removed, and the path must be recorded in `FilesRestored`.
4. Given a directory tracked as created, when rollback runs and the directory is empty, then
   it must be deleted; when it is non-empty, it must be left in place.

---

## L2-066: Rollback Ordering and Reporting
**Traces to:** L1-014

Rollback must reverse tracked actions in last-in-first-out order and must return a
`RollbackReport` listing files deleted, files restored, directories deleted, and any
failures. A failure to reverse one action must not abort the reversal of the others.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a directory was created before a file inside it, when rollback runs, then the file
   must be deleted before the directory.
2. Given one tracked file is locked by another process, when rollback runs, then the
   remaining actions must still be reversed and the failure must appear in
   `report.Failures` with the action and exception.
3. Given a rollback with two deletions and one restoration, when the report is inspected,
   then it must list two entries in `FilesDeleted` and one in `FilesRestored`.

---

## L2-067: Commit Finalizes a Generation Run
**Traces to:** L1-014

`Commit()` must make the run irreversible: subsequent `Rollback()` calls must do nothing,
and all backup files must be deleted. Backup cleanup must be best-effort and must not throw.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `Commit()` has been called, when `Rollback()` is called, then no file must be
   deleted or restored and the returned report must be empty.
2. Given `Commit()` is called after tracking a modified file, when the filesystem is
   inspected, then no `.bak.*` file must remain.
3. Given a backup file cannot be deleted during commit, when `Commit()` returns, then no
   exception must propagate.
4. Given a command handler completes successfully, when the handler exits, then `Commit()`
   must have been called; given it throws, `Rollback()` must have been called before the
   exception is rethrown.

---

## L2-068: Dry Run Writes Nothing
**Traces to:** L1-015

With `--dry-run`, no file or directory must be created, no external command must be
executed, and rollback must not be engaged.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `scaffold --dry-run` against a configuration declaring twelve files, when the
   command completes, then the output directory must contain no new file or directory.
2. Given `--dry-run`, when the run completes, then no post-scaffold command must have been
   executed.
3. Given `--dry-run` and a failure during planning, when the command completes, then rollback
   must not run.

---

## L2-069: Dry Run Reports the Full Plan
**Traces to:** L1-015

A dry run must report every file it would produce together with the action that would be
taken for it (for example create or overwrite).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a dry run over a configuration declaring twelve files, when the command completes,
   then twelve planned entries must be reported, each with a path and an action.
2. Given a planned file whose path already exists, when the plan is reported, then its action
   must indicate an overwrite rather than a create.
3. Given the same configuration is then run without `--dry-run`, when it completes, then the
   set of files created must equal the set previously reported.
4. Given planned files with known sizes, when the dry-run output is rendered, then sizes must
   be shown in human-readable units.

---

## L2-070: Command Suppression During Dry Run
**Traces to:** L1-015

`DryRunCommandService` must satisfy `ICommandService` without launching a process, recording
each suppressed command in the generation result instead.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `DryRunCommandService.Start("dotnet new sln -n X")`, when it is called, then no
   process must be started.
2. Given the same call, when the generation result is inspected, then the suppressed command
   must be recorded with its working directory.
3. Given `NoOpCommandService.Start(...)`, when it is called, then it must return without
   starting a process and without recording anything.

---

## L2-071: Terminal Detection Selects the Prompt Service
**Traces to:** L1-016

The CLI must register `SpectrePromptService` when standard input is attached to a terminal
and `NonInteractivePromptService` when input is redirected. `IsInteractive` must reflect
that decision.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given input is redirected (piped or from a file), when the CLI starts, then the resolved
   `IInteractivePromptService` must report `IsInteractive == false`.
2. Given an attached terminal, when the CLI starts, then the resolved prompt service must
   report `IsInteractive == true`.
3. Given a non-interactive session and a missing required option, when the command runs,
   then it must fail with a validation error rather than blocking on a prompt.

---

## L2-072: Prompting for Missing Options
**Traces to:** L1-016

In an interactive session, the root command must prompt for options that were not supplied,
seeding each prompt with the already-resolved value.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an interactive session and no `--name`, when the command runs, then the user must be
   prompted for the solution name and the entered value must be used.
2. Given an interactive session and `--name` supplied, when the command runs, then no prompt
   must be shown.
3. Given the user supplies a name at the prompt, when validation runs, then the prompted
   value must be subject to the same validation rules as a command-line value.

---

## L2-073: Interactive Configuration File Selection
**Traces to:** L1-016

When `scaffold` is run interactively without `--config` and no `scaffold.yaml` exists, the
CLI must offer the `*.yaml` and `*.yml` files in the output directory for selection.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an interactive session, no `--config`, no `scaffold.yaml`, and two `.yaml` files in
   the output directory, when the command runs, then both must be offered for selection.
2. Given the user selects one, when scaffolding proceeds, then that file must be used.
3. Given the directory contains no YAML files, when the command runs, then no prompt must be
   shown and the missing-configuration error must be reported.
4. Given a non-interactive session, when the same conditions hold, then no prompt must be
   shown.

---

## L2-074: Structured Console Rendering with Plain Fallback
**Traces to:** L1-017

`IConsoleRenderer` must expose headers, numbered step progress, success, error, warning and
info messages, a generated-file tree, and a run summary. A Spectre-based implementation
must be used when the terminal supports rich rendering and a plain-text implementation
otherwise, and both must present the same information.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given the rich renderer and a list of generated files, when the tree is written, then the
   directory hierarchy must be shown with each file under its parent directory.
2. Given the plain renderer and the same list, when the tree is written, then every file path
   must still appear in the output with no ANSI escape sequences.
3. Given a step count of 5, when step 3 is reported, then the output must indicate progress
   through step 3 of 5.
4. Given a completed run, when the summary is written, then it must state the number of files
   generated and the number of errors.

---

## L2-075: Human-Readable Size Formatting
**Traces to:** L1-017

Byte counts in generated output listings must be rendered in human-readable units.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `512`, when it is formatted, then the output must express the value in bytes.
2. Given `2048`, when it is formatted, then the output must express the value in kilobytes.
3. Given `5_242_880`, when it is formatted, then the output must express the value in
   megabytes.

---

## L2-076: Existing Project Type Detection
**Traces to:** L1-018

`IProjectContextFactory.Create(directory)` must classify an existing directory as DotNet,
Playwright, Detox, Angular, React Native, React, Flask, Python, or Unknown, based on the
marker files present, evaluated in that precedence order.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a directory containing a `.csproj`, when a context is created, then the detected
   type must be `DotNet`.
2. Given a directory containing `playwright.config.ts`, when a context is created, then the
   detected type must be `Playwright`.
3. Given a `package.json` whose content includes `"react-native"`, when a context is created,
   then the detected type must be `ReactNative` and not `React`.
4. Given a directory containing `app.py`, when a context is created, then the detected type
   must be `Flask`.
5. Given a directory that does not exist or contains no recognized marker, when a context is
   created, then the detected type must be `Unknown` and no exception must be thrown.

---

## L2-077: File Conflict Policy
**Traces to:** L1-018

Adding a file that already exists must be resolved by `IConflictResolver` under an explicit
policy of `Skip`, `Overwrite`, or `Error`. The default resolver must return `Error`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given the default resolver and an existing target file with differing content, when the
   conflict is resolved, then `ConflictAction.Error` must be returned.
2. Given a resolver configured to overwrite, when the conflict is resolved, then the existing
   file must be replaced with the new content.
3. Given a resolver configured to skip, when the conflict is resolved, then the existing file
   must be left byte-for-byte unchanged.
4. Given `--force` is supplied to `scaffold`, when an existing file is encountered, then it
   must be overwritten rather than reported as a conflict.

---

## L2-078: Incremental File Addition
**Traces to:** L1-018

`AddFileStrategy` must add a file to an existing project described by `AddFileModel`
without regenerating the project, honouring the conflict policy.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an existing project directory and an `AddFileModel` naming a new file, when the
   strategy runs, then only that file must be created and no existing file must be modified.
2. Given the target file already exists and the policy is `Error`, when the strategy runs,
   then the operation must fail identifying the conflicting path.
3. Given an `IncrementalProjectModel` listing three files to add, when generation runs, then
   all three must be added to the existing project.

---

## L2-079: Assembly Scanning Strategy Registration
**Traces to:** L1-019

`AddCoreServices(assembly)` must scan the supplied assembly for non-abstract
implementations of `IArtifactGenerationStrategy<>` and `ISyntaxGenerationStrategy<>` and
register each as a singleton against every matching closed interface. Types that cannot be
loaded must be skipped without aborting registration.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an assembly declaring a strategy for a custom model type, when
   `AddCoreServices(assembly)` is called, then resolving that closed strategy interface must
   return the implementation.
2. Given a strategy implementing two closed strategy interfaces, when registration runs, then
   it must be registered for both.
3. Given an assembly containing a type whose dependencies cannot be loaded, when registration
   runs, then registration must complete and the loadable strategies must still be
   registered.
4. Given an abstract strategy base class, when registration runs, then it must not be
   registered.

---

## L2-080: Plugin Assembly Discovery
**Traces to:** L1-019

`DirectoryPluginDiscovery` must search `<AppContext.BaseDirectory>/plugins` and
`<UserProfile>/.codegen/plugins` recursively for `*.dll`, and must tolerate missing
directories.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a DLL under `<BaseDirectory>/plugins/sub`, when discovery runs, then it must be
   reported with source `Directory`.
2. Given neither search path exists, when discovery runs, then an empty list must be returned
   and no exception must be thrown.
3. Given a DLL under `<UserProfile>/.codegen/plugins`, when discovery runs, then it must be
   reported.

---

## L2-081: Composite and Explicit Plugin Sources
**Traces to:** L1-019

`CompositePluginDiscovery` must aggregate the results of every registered discovery source,
including `ExplicitPluginDiscovery` for paths named by the caller, and a failure in one
source must not suppress the results of the others.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a directory source yielding two plugins and an explicit source yielding one, when
   composite discovery runs, then all three must be returned.
2. Given one source throws, when composite discovery runs, then the remaining sources' results
   must still be returned.
3. Given the same assembly path is reported by two sources, when composite discovery runs,
   then it must not be loaded twice.

---

## L2-082: Verification Step Sequencing
**Traces to:** L1-020

`VerificationRunner` must run every registered `IPostGenerationVerifier` and record a
per-step result. If the `dotnet build` verifier fails, every subsequent verifier must be
recorded as skipped with the reason `Skipped: build failed` rather than being executed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given three verifiers where `dotnet build` passes, when verification runs, then all three
   must execute and three results must be recorded.
2. Given `dotnet build` fails, when verification continues, then the remaining verifiers must
   not execute and each must be recorded with `Passed == false`, reason
   `Skipped: build failed`, and zero duration.
3. Given each executed verifier, when its result is recorded, then the result must carry the
   verifier name and its elapsed duration.

---

## L2-083: Verification Options
**Traces to:** L1-020

Verification must accept a required solution directory, an optional project path, a
warnings-as-errors switch defaulting to enabled, and a timeout defaulting to 120 seconds.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given no explicit timeout, when options are constructed, then `Timeout` must be 120
   seconds.
2. Given no explicit setting, when options are constructed, then `TreatWarningsAsErrors` must
   be `true`.
3. Given a verifier exceeds the configured timeout, when verification completes, then that
   step must be recorded as failed with a timeout reason.
4. Given `SolutionDirectory` is not supplied, when options are constructed, then construction
   must fail.

---

## L2-084: Dependency Manifest Resolution
**Traces to:** L1-021

`IDependencyResolver` must resolve a package version for a framework key by consulting a
manifest on disk beside the executing assembly first, then an embedded resource, and must
throw `FileNotFoundException` naming both searched locations when neither exists. Loaded
manifests must be cached per framework key.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a manifest on disk for framework key `net9.0`, when `GetVersion("net9.0", "Serilog")`
   is called, then the disk value must be returned.
2. Given no disk manifest but an embedded manifest for the key, when the version is
   requested, then the embedded value must be returned.
3. Given neither manifest exists, when the version is requested, then
   `FileNotFoundException` must be thrown naming the disk path and the resource name.
4. Given a package absent from an existing manifest, when its version is requested, then
   `KeyNotFoundException` must be thrown naming the package and the manifest.
5. Given the same framework key is resolved twice, when the second call is made, then the
   manifest must not be re-read from disk.

---

## L2-085: Package Version Consistency
**Traces to:** L1-021

The versions the CLI stamps into generated `PackageReference` entries must be maintained in
a single location (`PackageVersions`), must be semantic-version formatted, and must match
the versions actually published for those packages.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given each constant in `PackageVersions`, when it is inspected, then it must be non-empty
   and must match `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+`.
2. Given `PackageVersions.AsTokenDictionary()`, when it is produced, then it must contain one
   `package_version_*` token per generator package.
3. Given the version declared in each `src/**/*.csproj`, when it is compared with the
   corresponding `PackageVersions` constant, then the two must be equal.
   **Status: Gap** — `PackageVersions.Core` is `1.3.0` while `CodeGenerator.Core.csproj`
   publishes `1.3.1`; the CI version-bump step updates the `.csproj` without updating
   `PackageVersions`.

---

## L2-086: Local Source Redirection for Generated Projects
**Traces to:** L1-021

A generated project must reference CodeGenerator either by `PackageReference` at pinned
versions or, when `--local-source-root` is supplied, by `ProjectReference` paths computed
relative to the generated project directory.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `--local-source-root ../../CodeGenerator/src`, when the `.csproj` is generated, then
   it must contain nine `ProjectReference` entries with paths relative to the generated
   project directory.
2. Given no `--local-source-root`, when the `.csproj` is generated, then it must contain nine
   `PackageReference` entries and no `ProjectReference`.
3. Given `--local-source-root` points at a directory that does not contain the referenced
   projects, when the generated solution is built, then the build failure must name the
   unresolved project path.

---

## L2-087: Transient I/O Retry
**Traces to:** L1-022

`Retry.ExecuteAsync` must retry an operation that fails with a transient exception, applying
an exponential backoff bounded by a maximum delay, up to a configured attempt limit; it must
not retry non-transient failures. `IOException` is transient except for
`FileNotFoundException` and `DirectoryNotFoundException`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an operation that throws `IOException` twice and then succeeds with a limit of three
   attempts, when it is executed, then it must succeed and must have been invoked three
   times.
2. Given an operation that throws `FileNotFoundException`, when it is executed, then it must
   fail immediately after one invocation.
3. Given an operation that always throws a transient exception, when the attempt limit is
   exhausted, then the last exception must be rethrown.
4. Given a backoff multiplier and a maximum delay, when successive retries occur, then no
   delay must exceed the maximum delay.
5. Given the cancellation token is cancelled between attempts, when the next attempt is due,
   then `OperationCanceledException` must be thrown instead.

---

## L2-088: Cancellation Wiring
**Traces to:** L1-022

The CLI must intercept Ctrl+C, cancel the shared `CancellationTokenSource` instead of
terminating abruptly, and thread that token through commands, the artifact generator, and
the scaffold engine.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given Ctrl+C is pressed during generation, when the handler runs, then the default
   terminate behaviour must be suppressed and the token must be cancelled.
2. Given the token is cancelled, when generation observes it, then the process must exit with
   code `8` after writing `Operation cancelled.` to standard error.
3. Given cancellation occurs mid-run and the run is not a dry run, when the handler unwinds,
   then already-created files must be left as-is rather than rolled back, because
   `OperationCanceledException` is excluded from the rollback handler.

---

## L2-089: Cross-Platform Command Execution
**Traces to:** L1-022

`ICommandService.Start` must execute a command through `cmd.exe /C` on Windows and
`bash -c` on Linux and macOS, defaulting the working directory to the current directory,
returning the process exit code when waiting for exit, and observing cancellation before
launch.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a command and no working directory on Windows, when it is started, then it must be
   launched through `cmd.exe /C` in the current directory.
2. Given the same on Linux, when it is started, then it must be launched through `bash -c`.
3. Given `waitForExit` is `true` and the command exits with code `2`, when `Start` returns,
   then the return value must be `2`.
4. Given an already-cancelled token, when `Start` is called, then
   `OperationCanceledException` must be thrown and no process must be launched.

---

## L2-090: Path Traversal Prevention
**Traces to:** L1-023

No caller-supplied path must be permitted to escape the output tree. Project paths, directory paths, and
template relative paths containing `..` must be rejected, and `CommonRules.IsValidFilePath`
must return `false` for them.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a scaffold project with `path: ../../etc`, when the configuration is validated, then
   an error naming path traversal must be reported and no file must be written.
2. Given a scaffold directory definition containing `..`, when the configuration is
   validated, then a path-traversal error must be reported.
3. Given a discovered template whose relative path contains `..`, when discovery runs, then
   the template must be skipped and a warning must be logged.
4. Given a path containing `..`, when `CommonRules.IsValidFilePath` is called, then it must
   return `false`.
5. Given an absolute path outside the resolved output root, when a file write is attempted,
   then the write must be refused. **Status: Gap** — traversal is blocked by `..` string
   matching only; absolute paths and symbolic links are not currently checked.

---

## L2-091: Post-Scaffold Command Trust Boundary
**Traces to:** L1-023

Commands declared in a scaffold configuration are executed through the system shell. The
system must treat a configuration file as untrusted input: it must require explicit
confirmation or an explicit opt-in flag before executing `postScaffoldCommands` originating
from a configuration the invoking user did not author.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a configuration declaring `postScaffoldCommands`, when scaffolding runs
   non-interactively without an execution opt-in, then the commands must not be executed and
   the skip must be reported.
2. Given the execution opt-in is supplied, when scaffolding runs, then the commands must be
   executed in the resolved output root.
3. Given an interactive session and a configuration declaring commands, when scaffolding
   reaches the post-scaffold phase, then the commands must be displayed and confirmed before
   execution.

**Status: Gap** — `PostScaffoldExecutor` currently executes declared commands unconditionally
whenever the run is not a dry run.

---

## L2-092: Plugin Load Trust
**Traces to:** L1-023

Assemblies discovered from the plugin directories must be loaded only after the system has
established they are intended to be loaded, and a plugin that fails to load must be reported
with error code `PLUGIN_LOAD_FAILED` without terminating the run.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a DLL in the plugin directory that is not a valid managed assembly, when discovery
   and loading run, then an error with code `PLUGIN_LOAD_FAILED` must be recorded and the
   run must continue.
2. Given a plugin whose strategy throws during generation, when the run completes, then the
   failure must be attributed to that plugin's strategy and other strategies must still have
   executed.
3. Given plugin loading is not explicitly enabled, when the CLI starts, then assemblies from
   the plugin directories must not be loaded. **Status: Gap** — discovery enumerates plugin
   directories with no opt-in or integrity check.

---

## L2-093: Secret Non-Disclosure
**Traces to:** L1-023

Configuration values, environment variables, and diagnostics output must not disclose
secrets. Values sourced from environment variables must be redacted in diagnostic and
verbose output, and generated `.env` files must not be populated with real credentials.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given an environment variable mapped into configuration, when `--diagnostics` output is
   rendered, then its value must be redacted rather than printed.
2. Given `--verbose` logging, when configuration is resolved, then no configuration value
   must be written to the log at `Debug` level in cleartext.
3. Given a generated `.env` file, when it is inspected, then every secret-bearing key must
   carry a placeholder value.

**Status: Gap** — no redaction is currently applied to configuration or diagnostics output.

---

## L2-094: Reflection Caching
**Traces to:** L1-024

Both `ArtifactGenerator` and `SyntaxGenerator` must construct the generic dispatch delegate
for a model type at most once per process and serve subsequent calls from a concurrent
cache.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given 1,000 generations of the same model type, when the run completes, then the generic
   dispatch method must have been constructed exactly once for that type.
2. Given concurrent generation of the same model type from multiple threads, when the run
   completes, then no duplicate cache entry must be created and no exception must be thrown.
3. Given generation of 1,000 models of one type, when total elapsed time is compared with
   generation of 100 models of the same type, then the per-model cost must not increase.

---

## L2-095: Object and String Buffer Caching
**Traces to:** L1-024

The system must reuse pooled `StringBuilder` instances for syntax composition and must cache
resolved objects through `IObjectCache` rather than recomputing them per artifact.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given repeated syntax generation, when `StringBuilderCache` is used, then a released
   builder must be reused by the next acquisition on the same thread.
2. Given a builder larger than the pool's maximum retained capacity, when it is released,
   then it must not be retained.
3. Given the same key is requested twice from `IObjectCache`, when the second request is
   made, then the cached instance must be returned without recomputation.

---

## L2-096: Template and Manifest Caching
**Traces to:** L1-024

Discovered template plans, registered styles, and dependency manifests must be resolved once
and reused for the remainder of the process.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a dependency manifest already loaded for a framework key, when it is requested
   again, then no filesystem or resource read must occur.
2. Given styles have been discovered for a templates root, when a style is requested, then it
   must be served from the registry without re-enumerating the filesystem.
3. Given a generation run producing 100 files from one template set, when the run completes,
   then each template file must have been read from disk at most once.

---

## L2-097: Correlation Identifier
**Traces to:** L1-025

Every CLI invocation must generate a correlation identifier, publish it on
`DiagnosticContext.Current`, and attach it to the results it produces.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given the root command runs, when generation begins, then
   `DiagnosticContext.Current.CorrelationId` must be a non-empty unique value.
2. Given the `scaffold` command runs, when the `ScaffoldResult` is produced, then its
   `CorrelationId` must equal the value on the diagnostic context.
3. Given two sequential invocations, when their correlation identifiers are compared, then
   they must differ.

---

## L2-098: Diagnostics Report
**Traces to:** L1-025

With `--diagnostics`, the CLI must time each generation step and render a report containing
the execution environment (including the CLI version) and every timed step with its
duration and the total elapsed time. Without the flag, timing must be disabled with no
measurable overhead.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given `--diagnostics`, when the command completes, then a report listing each named step
   with its duration and a total duration must be rendered.
2. Given `--diagnostics`, when the report is rendered, then it must include the runtime
   version, operating system, and CLI version.
3. Given no `--diagnostics`, when the command runs, then a no-op timer must be used and no
   report must be rendered.
4. Given `scaffold --validate --diagnostics`, when the command completes, then the report
   must be rendered even though nothing was written.

---

## L2-099: Structured Logging
**Traces to:** L1-025

All progress, warnings, and failures must be emitted through `ILogger` with structured
message templates and named placeholders rather than pre-formatted strings.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given generation begins, when the log entry is emitted, then it must use a message
   template with a named placeholder for the model type.
2. Given a validation warning, when it is logged, then the property name and message must be
   separate structured values.
3. Given `--verbose`, when the run executes, then `Debug`-level entries from the strategy
   executor must be emitted.

---

## L2-100: NuGet Package Identity
**Traces to:** L1-026

Each publishable component must ship as a NuGet package under the `QuinntyneBrown.` prefix
with an explicit `PackageId` and `Version`, and non-publishable projects must be marked
`IsPackable=false`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given each publishable project in `src/`, when its `.csproj` is inspected, then it must
   declare a `PackageId` beginning with `QuinntyneBrown.CodeGenerator.` and a `Version`.
2. Given each test project, when its `.csproj` is inspected, then it must declare
   `IsPackable=false`.
3. Given the CI publish step, when it selects projects to pack, then projects lacking a
   `PackageId` or marked non-packable must be skipped.

---

## L2-101: Global Tool Packaging
**Traces to:** L1-026

`CodeGenerator.Cli` must pack as a .NET global tool with `ToolCommandName` `create-code-cli`
and `PackageId` `QuinntyneBrown.CodeGenerator.Cli`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given the CLI project, when its `.csproj` is inspected, then `PackAsTool` must be `true`
   and `ToolCommandName` must be `create-code-cli`.
2. Given the packed tool is installed with `dotnet tool install -g`, when `create-code-cli`
   is invoked with no arguments, then the root command help must be displayed.
3. Given the tool is installed, when `create-code-cli scaffold --help` is invoked, then the
   scaffold command options must be listed.

---

## L2-102: Release Automation
**Traces to:** L1-026

On every push to `main` the pipeline must restore, build the solution in Release, and run
the unit tests. It must detect changed packable projects, bump their patch version, pack,
publish to NuGet with duplicates skipped, and commit the version bump with a message that
does not retrigger the pipeline, and it must perform none of those steps unless the build
and tests have passed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given a push where the build fails, when the workflow runs, then the publish job must not
   execute.
2. Given a push touching only `docs/`, when the workflow runs, then no package must be packed
   or published.
3. Given a push touching `src/CodeGenerator.Core`, when the publish job runs, then that
   project's patch version must be incremented and the package must be pushed to NuGet.
4. Given a version bump is committed, when the commit message is inspected, then it must
   contain `[skip ci]`.
5. Given a package version already present on NuGet, when publish runs, then the push must be
   skipped rather than failing the job.

---

## L2-103: Unit Test Coverage per Component
**Traces to:** L1-027

Every `src/` package must have a corresponding unit test project, and every unit test project
must compile and run in CI.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given each package in `src/` other than the CLI shells, when the test tree is inspected,
   then a matching `tests/<Package>.UnitTests` project must exist.
2. Given each test project, when the solution is built, then it must compile without error.
3. Given each test project, when its sources are inspected, then the xUnit test framework
   must be resolvable in every test file.
4. Given the CI test step, when it runs, then it must execute every unit test project rather
   than a single project. **Status: Gap** — CI currently runs only
   `CodeGenerator.Core.UnitTests`, so failures in other test projects surface only as build
   errors.

---

## L2-104: Integration Test Coverage per Feature Area
**Traces to:** L1-027

Each cross-cutting feature area must be covered by an integration test suite exercising it
end to end, including YAML scaffolding, configuration hierarchy, dry run, rollback, plugin
discovery, error handling, template discovery and filters, schema normalization, diagnostics,
verification, resilience, and shell completion.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given each feature area listed above, when the integration test project is inspected, then
   at least one test class covering it must exist.
2. Given the integration suite, when it runs against a temporary directory, then it must not
   modify the repository working tree.
3. Given the integration suite, when it completes, then every temporary directory it created
   must have been removed.

---

## L2-105: Acceptance Test Traceability
**Traces to:** L1-027

Every acceptance test must declare, in a comment header, the L2 requirements it covers, and
every L2 requirement must be covered by at least one acceptance test before the requirement
is considered implemented.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Given any acceptance test file, when its header is inspected, then it must contain a
   `Traces to:` line naming one or more L2 identifiers.
2. Given a `Traces to:` line, when each identifier is checked, then it must correspond to a
   requirement declared in this document.
3. Given the full L2 set, when coverage is computed, then every requirement not marked
   **Status: Gap** must be referenced by at least one acceptance test.
